raw_response:
I'm 42, been farming these 10 mu for 20 years. My family has four people — my husband works at a tile factory in town, my daughter is in high school, my son is in middle school and helps when he's free. We have 8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and I keep 2.1 mu of cotton on the south plot for extra cash. Cotton is labor-intensive but last year the price was okay, so I keep it.

For the wheat I planted last October, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now it's jointing stage, I'll topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. The extension technician told me some farmers use 20 kg, but last year I used about 15 kg and got around 420 kg per mu, which is decent. I don't want to waste money — if I put too much and it rains too much, it lodges anyway. I'll irrigate three times total: the winter irrigation was done in November, I irrigated at green-up in March, and now I'll irrigate once more at jointing if it doesn't rain. Pumping costs about 30 yuan each time, so I don't water unless I have to. I'll spray herbicide for weeds and keep an eye out for disease.

For cotton, I'll plant around April 22nd after plowing. I buy hybrid seed, about 70 yuan per mu. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress with urea when it flowers. The main worry is bollworm — I'll spray insecticide four or five times. I'll need to hire people to help pick in September and October, about eight days total, paying roughly 120 yuan per day. My family will pick too.

For maize, after wheat harvest in early June, we have maybe five days to plant. I'll buy hybrid seed — probably Zhengdan 958, it's reliable. Put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 40 kg per mu. Then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage, around 20 kg per mu. Maize doesn't need much water here if the summer rains come, but I'll irrigate once at silking if it's dry. That one irrigation is crucial. I'm hoping for 480 kg per mu this year if the weather is good.

My total input costs will be about 8,600 yuan. My husband's wage helps, but we need to save for my daughter's school fees and for emergencies. I thought about dropping cotton to save labor, but the cotton income is good insurance if grain prices drop.
